name: Blue Raven
author: Enterrahost

sections.description:
Most form plugins email you. A few can text you. Almost none of them also keep what was sent, or let you undo a clean-up. Blue Raven does all three, and adds the search tools that usually need three more plugins.

Mail, Text and Archive. A form builder with every field type a real contact form needs, a delivery screen that tests your SMTP and your SMS before a visitor does, and an archive of every entry that survives a bounced email. Entries older than 90 days are removed on a schedule, and the tables are snapshotted first, so a wrong click costs a restore rather than a lost lead.

Undo what other plugins leave behind. Deactivated plugins leave options, transients, cron events and tables that nothing else will ever clean. Defrag lists them, says what each one belongs to, takes a snapshot, and removes what you choose. It checks again before touching anything, so a plugin switched back on is never guessed at.

The search tools, all in one place. Meta titles and descriptions with a live preview, a content score that says what is missing rather than only how much, schema, robots.txt, an XML sitemap, IndexNow, redirects that refuse to save a loop, per-template noindex, verification codes, analytics tags and llms.txt.

Every tool is off until you turn it on. Nothing is published, rewritten or sent because you installed it. If another SEO plugin is already emitting tags, Blue Raven says so and stands down instead of writing a second set.

No account, no licence server. Nothing about your site is sent to Enterrahost. The only outbound calls are the ones a tool you switched on exists to make: a URL to IndexNow, a form’s answers to your own mail server, an SMS body to your vendor, page views to the analytics account you named.

A full walkthrough of every screen is on the plugin’s own page, and the changelog below says what each release changed.

External services

Every one of these is off until you switch it on, and each is called only by the tool that needs it. There is no account with Enterrahost and no licence check.

Search and analytics

  • IndexNow — a changed URL, sent to Bing and Yandex when you save a page. Terms
  • Google Analytics — page views, on your own measurement ID. Terms
  • Microsoft Clarity — session and heatmap data, on your own project ID. Terms
  • Meta Pixel — page views, on your own pixel ID. Terms
  • Ahrefs — the analytics key you paste in. Terms

Spam protection

  • Cloudflare Turnstile Terms, reCAPTCHA Terms and hCaptcha Terms — a token check on form submit, only on forms you protect.

Text messages

The SMS body goes to Twilio Terms, SMSPortal Terms or Clickatell Terms, whichever you configure, on your own account.

AI writing

DeepSeek — a key you add yourself through WordPress’s Connectors screen. Nothing is sent unless you tick that provider. Terms

Your host’s mail server sends the form notifications, and this site’s own database stores the entries.

Privacy. Each service’s own policy governs what it receives: Microsoft (IndexNow and Clarity), Google (Analytics and reCAPTCHA), Meta, Ahrefs, Cloudflare, hCaptcha, Twilio, SMSPortal, Clickatell and DeepSeek. Privacy: https://enterrahost.com/privacy/ for this plugin itself.

Consent. If a consent manager is present, a tracking tag waits for it: WordPress’s Consent API through wp_has_consent and wp_listen_for_consent_change, Complianz through its own cmplz_status_change event, and Cookiebot through CookiebotOnAccept. The functional category is never gated, because the forms themselves are what the visitor came to use; statistics and marketing are. Blue Raven is a consumer of consent, not a provider of it: it ships no cookie banner, asks nobody and keeps no consent record of its own — whatever your manager decides is what it obeys. With no manager installed nothing stops them from running, which is what you asked for by switching the tag on.

Importing from another plugin

Forms -> Import lists the forms Contact Form 7 and Ninja Forms hold, with their fields and where they are used, and creates a new Blue Raven form from one you choose. Nothing is written to the other plugin, and no page changes during an import.

What imports. Field type, key, label, required star and choice options are carried across, including CF7’s [acceptance] sentence and Ninja’s textbox, listselect, listradio, listcheckbox and phone types. Keys are kept where the source has a stable one.

What does not. A file upload, a calculation, conditional logic, multi-step navigation, payment fields and Ninja’s rating fields have no equivalent here; the import names them rather than dropping them silently, and the form is created without them. Ninja choice options stored in its field meta are not read yet, so a Ninja dropdown can arrive with no choices.

Swapping the shortcode is optional and separate. It replaces the other plugin’s shortcode with [blue_raven_form id="N"] only on pages whose content contains a reference this plugin can rewrite — a quoted shortcode, a bare id=, or the CF7 block. It records the exact text it replaced before changing anything, and Undo restores that text per page, even if the imported form is later deleted. A page edited after the swap is left alone by Undo, so later work is never overwritten.

Where the swap will not reach. Forms embedded by a widget, a builder element or a template file are found and reported but not edited: Elementor, Bricks and Beaver Builder keep their content in post meta JSON, widgets keep theirs in an option, and a theme that calls do_shortcode() in PHP is invisible to any database query. Those need one manual edit. Divi, WPBakery and Flatsome’s UX Builder store shortcodes in the post body and are swapped normally.

Pages, not templates. The swap edits post content. A shortcode inside a page template, a header/footer builder layout saved outside the post, or a reusable block that has already been rendered into a page may need its source edited instead.
sections.faq:
Does it change my theme or my SEO plugin?

No. It writes no CSS to your site, emits no tags when another SEO plugin is already doing that, and every tool ships switched off. Turn on what you want and it stays out of the way of the rest.

Does it contact any server?

Only what a tool you switched on exists to send: a URL to IndexNow, a form’s answers to your own mail server, an SMS body to the vendor you chose, page-view data to the analytics account you named. There is no account and no licence check.

How does the AI writing work, and whose key is it?

Yours. A key added under Settings, Connectors stays in WordPress; Blue Raven can only use a provider you tick, and it sends nothing unless you press the button.

What search tools are included?

Meta tags, a content score, schema, robots.txt, an XML sitemap, IndexNow, redirects, noindex rules, analytics tags, verification codes and llms.txt for AI crawlers.

What does this release not do?

It does not optimise images, generate body copy, or run its own AI service. The full list, and the longer answers to the questions above, is under “How the tools work”.
sections.changelog:
2.1.2

  • Added: Content -> Images. Lists images by alt-text state, paginated, opening on the ones with none. Filters for no alt text, decorative, has alt text, and all. Each row has a field that writes WordPress’s own alt meta, so an image can be fixed without leaving the screen.
  • Added: a link from Meta to the Noindex screen, so “what is noindexed” is one click from the switch that decides it.
  • Fixed: the copy button on the content table copies from the page itself rather than a request, so it works on the first click; it no longer falls back to downloading the markdown file.
  • Fixed: an image with no alt row and an image with an empty alt are now told apart. “Decorative” means somebody saved an empty alt; “not set” means nobody looked.

2.1.1

  • Fixed: a form message cleared on purpose was stored as an empty string, so a visitor who submitted saw a notice box with nothing in it — or, on failure, no explanation at all. Success, failure and blocked each fall back to the sentence the plugin ships.
  • Added: those three defaults are shown as placeholders in the form builder, so the wording is visible before anyone saves.

2.1.0

  • Added: import from Contact Form 7 and Ninja Forms. Forms -> Import lists what the other plugin holds, with each form’s fields and how many pages already use it, and creates a new Blue Raven form from the one you pick. Nothing is written to the other plugin and no page changes during an import.
  • Added: optional shortcode swap. Where a page still carries the other plugin’s shortcode, the import offers to replace it with this plugin’s on those pages only, records the exact text it replaced first, and can undo the swap per import — including after the imported form is deleted.
  • Added: “Submissions per address” on Delivery — a per-form, per-address limit for a rolling ten minutes, default 8, 0 turns it off. Refused submissions are counted with the other blocked attempts.
  • Added: a form submission now spends its bot stamp once, so a harvested stamp can no longer be replayed for its whole two-hour window.
  • Added: the import list reports fields it cannot map (file uploads, calculations, conditional logic) instead of dropping them quietly.
  • Added: outbound links beside the verification fields (Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, Meta Business, Ahrefs) and on the sitemap, IndexNow and robots sections, so the code being asked for can be fetched from the screen that asks.
  • Fixed: the From address was only applied when the SMTP switch was on, so form mail and every test button still left as wordpress@your-domain. It now applies to all four send paths.
  • Fixed: a From name containing a line break could add a second mail header. Header values are flattened before they become headers.
  • Fixed: the buttons said SEND because a theme uppercases buttons; the label keeps the case it was given.
  • Fixed: “Send the test” reloaded to Overview and hid its own result. It returns to Delivery with the result shown.
  • Fixed: Width and Alignment were only available with a custom style, though they apply in every mode.
  • Fixed: a field set to “Half — right” came back as full width after every save.
  • Fixed: the Advanced CSS box was visible in every mode, because an attribute was losing to a display rule, and its Load button loaded the saved stub instead of the sheet.
  • Fixed: submitting a form with a required field empty cleared every field and answered with one generic sentence. The browser now checks first, so nothing is lost.
  • Fixed: a thank-you message was shown twice, and the form stayed on screen under it. The form steps aside and offers “Send another message”.
  • Fixed: the result message stayed in the address bar, so a reload re-reported an old error or an old success.
  • Fixed: the WP-Cron warning never cleared, even on a server running cron on time. It clears once a real run is seen.
  • Fixed: form help text was not connected to its input for screen readers (aria-describedby).
  • Fixed: the “Needs attention” From-address link pointed at a screen without that field.
  • Changed: the WP-Cron, sitemap and robots warnings now name the action to take and link to it.

2.0.1

  • Fixed: opening the AI screen on a site where AI was still switched off showed a white page and logged a fatal — “Undefined constant BlueRaven\Ai\BLUE_RAVEN_AI_CRON_HOOK”. The settings screen that turns AI on now loads before the switch is on.
  • Fixed: saving that screen answered “The et_ai_group options page is not in the allowed options list”, for the same reason — the setting was only registered once AI was already enabled.
  • Fixed: a dropdown’s list could open behind the card below it on Schema. The panel now leaves the card while open, so nothing can cover it.
  • Fixed: “Add a contact point” produced a Serves field that was a scrolling multi-select rather than a searchable list.
  • Added: “Start fresh” beside the 1.x import prompt, so a site with nothing worth carrying over can say so. Neither answer deletes anything, and both now confirm what happened.

2.0.0

  • Blue Raven. The plugin is renamed from EnterraTools, with the same screens under a new menu name.
  • Requires WordPress 7.0 and PHP 8.0.
  • Upgrading from 1.x is a decision, not a side effect: the settings, the hand-written titles and the forms are carried over only after you press the button on the dashboard. The old tables are never deleted.
  • AI writing on a key you already own, through WordPress’s own Connectors screen. The DeepSeek connector is offered by a switch and is off by default.
  • A content score beside the SEO score — in the editor, in the list table and on the dashboard — with a checklist that says what is missing rather than only how much.
  • Header and footer scripts as a list: a name, a place, a consent category, defer or async, and an order you set.
  • Site Defrag can sweep expired transients on a window you choose, and restore a quarantined table with one click.
  • New: a “delete all data” switch, so deleting the plugin can remove its records — or not.
  • EnterraMon and EnterraSEO verification keys on the Verification screen.
  • Resend any archived submission, to the form’s own recipient or to another address. The entry keeps the address the customer wrote from; the resend is added to its note.
  • Noindex rules for the pages that should never rank — cart, checkout, my account, search, author archives, 404s, attachments, page two onwards — with a Noindex screen that lists them and a tick for a single page.
  • Archive pages now get a description and social tags, and a page with no featured image falls back to a default share image instead of shipping no image at all.
  • A textarea keeps its line breaks in the mail and in the archive. One long message is no longer flattened to a single line.
  • Cloudflare Turnstile, with light, dark or automatic widget theming.
  • Send a test message from the SMTP card and a test text from the SMS card, answered in place without reloading the page.
  • Each form has its own “text somebody when this form is sent” switch, greyed out when the site has no SMS provider.
  • The IndexNow key URL answers 200 directly, without a redirect.
  • Profiles and extra contact points on the Schema screen are one field per entry, rather than a line format you had to be told.

0.3.1

  • “Redirect this” on a 404 row: it pre-fills the add-rule form with the missing path
    rather than creating a rule silently, so the target stays your choice and the loop
    check still runs.
  • The 404 log is filterable by verdict — Break, Wrong URL, Probe — with counts, ten
    rows a page.
  • Fixed: two strings reused the same placeholder pattern with mismatched translator
    comments, which the gate now refuses.

0.3.0

  • Redirects: exact and prefix matching, 301/302/410, priority order, and loops refused
    at save with the path shown — not discovered in production.
  • Chains collapse: A to B to C answers A straight to C, once.
  • A link snapshot: every URL the site ever published is recorded, and never pruned, so a
    404 can be told apart from a broken link, a mistyped address and a scanner probe.
  • 404 log with three verdicts — Break, Wrong URL, Probe — and its own retention (90 days).
  • One screen per job: Delivery settings is split into Sending, Anti-spam, Text alerts and
    Archive, and the admin menu is grouped into four sections with labels that never wrap.
  • reCAPTCHA v3, with the score threshold that makes it a check rather than a formality.
  • The dashboard gauge: setup (tools switched on) and health (checks passing) scored apart,
    so a site with nothing on cannot read 100.
  • Fixed: at 390px the whole admin scrolled sideways, because two grid floors were wider
    than a phone’s content area.

0.2.0 (folded)

  • Sitemap, IndexNow and the redirect manager.

0.1.0

  • First release. Meta tags, schema and robots.txt.

2.0.1

Fixes a fatal on the AI screen when AI was not yet switched on, and a Save that could not register its own settings. Update from 2.0.0 is a straight file swap; nothing migrates.

2.0.0

A major version. On a site that ran 1.x, nothing is imported until you press “Import my Blue Raven 1.x data” on the dashboard — the old tables are untouched and the new tools are off until then. Take a backup first.

upgrade_notice.2.1.2: Shows what the thin-pages switch actually noindexes, with a live URL for each rule and any page ticked by hand.
upgrade_notice.2.1.1: Fixes blank form messages: a success, failure or blocked message left empty now falls back to the plugin's own sentence instead of showing an empty box to the visitor.
upgrade_notice.2.1.0: Adds importing from Contact Form 7 and Ninja Forms, with an optional and reversible shortcode swap, plus a submission limit per address. Importing reads the other plugin and writes nothing to it. Take a backup before swapping shortcodes on live pages.
upgrade_notice.2.0.1: Fixes a fatal on the AI screen when AI was not yet switched on, a Save there that could not register its own settings, and a Content-Signal line that was missing from robots.txt unless AI writing was also on.

screenshots.caption: The dashboard: what is live, what needs attention, and the AI calls left today.
Readiness: what a search engine will find, and what is standing in the way.
Meta: the title, the description and the social tags, with a preview as you type.
Content score: what a page is missing, not only how much it has.
Schema: organization, website and page markup from a few fields.
robots.txt: the rules WordPress serves, and what a crawler actually gets.
AI and llms.txt: the provider, the daily cap and what is being published.
Writing: the providers Blue Raven may call, and the model chosen for each.
Header and footer: scripts in the head or before the body, with a consent gate.
Redirects: rules that refuse to save a loop.
Analytics: one switch per provider, on your own account.
Forms: the form list, with entries and delivery in reach.
The form builder: fields on the left, a live preview on the right.
Defrag: what other plugins left behind, and a snapshot before it goes.
Archive: every entry, kept after a bounced email or a quiet day.
